title: Perfect matchings in trees via odd components
statement: Let $G$ be a finite tree, and for a graph $H$ write $o(H)$ for the number of connected components of $H$ having an odd number of vertices. Then $G$ has a perfect matching if and only if $o(G - v) = 1$ for every vertex $v$ of $G$, where $G - v$ denotes the graph obtained from $G$ by deleting $v$ together with all edges incident to it.
hypotheses_covered: conclusion: G has a perfect matching iff for every vertex v the number of odd components of G minus v equals 1
